headline: Two shell-capable coding agents share the workspace and git state — high capability conflict and prompt-injection risk via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents read repository files and treat tool-result content as input to subsequent steps. Files written by Cursor's Agent (or Yolo-mode commands) become input the next time Claude Code reads them, and vice versa, with no provenance tracking. A malicious or model-confused string in a generated comment can hijack the other agent's next planning step.
mitigations: Keep one agent read-only when both are running
Use git worktrees to give each agent a separate working tree

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents send file contents to vendor inference backends (Anthropic for Claude Code, model proxies for Cursor). The same source — including secrets that landed in tracked files — flows to two separate vendors with different retention. Cursor offers Privacy Mode but it is not the default for free accounts.
mitigations: Add a pre-commit hook that scans for secrets
Restrict each agent to disjoint subdirectories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both have unrestricted filesystem write and modify git state without coordination. Two simultaneous agents staging or committing in the same repo can clobber each other's working tree, lose unsaved edits, or push half-applied changes.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to commit or stage to the same git branch concurrently
mitigations: Run agents on separate git worktrees or branches
Require manual review before any commit
Stop one agent before invoking the other for the same file

D_cascading_error.rationale: Each can act on the other's outputs as ground truth (a Claude Code refactor becomes the file Cursor inlines tests against). With no automatic verification step between them, a confident hallucination from one can be entrenched by the other's commit.
mitigations: Require human review of each diff

E_compliance.rationale: Both vendors document data handling and Cursor offers a Privacy Mode, but using both creates two separate processor relationships for the same code, which an enterprise DPA review will flag.
mitigations: Confirm both vendors are covered by your enterprise DPA
Document the dual-processor flow in your AI inventory
